The most powerful refutation is that it is impossible to calculate all the consequences of one's acts. The calculus requires summing the pleasures and pains of every consequence, including far-reaching and unforeseeable ones, so it cannot be applied in practice. The "inevitable pain" option doesn't touch the calculus's method, and this replaces my earlier answer about commensurability, which wasn't one of the options.

CONFIDENCE: 72
